title: Basis of Settlement on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
## 1. What a benefit is measured against

1.1 Each benefit of a Travel Protection Plans certificate has its own limit. Cancellation and interruption are shares of the declared trip cost. Medical, evacuation and accident benefits are amounts per insured traveller. Baggage, delay and rental benefits are amounts per traveller with their own inner ceilings per article or per day.

1.2 Benefit already paid in this policy term is deducted from the limit before the payment is made, so limits are consumed across the term rather than restored claim by claim: benefit limits are consumed across the policy term.

1.3 A cancel-for-any-reason claim is paid at the plan's own reimbursement share of the trip cost and never at the full cancellation share.

## 2. What is withheld

2.1 The deductible withheld is the one the benefit names, and where the benefit names none the plan's general deductible is withheld.

## 3. How the money reaches the traveller

3.1 Payment is made to the policyholder in the currency the premium was paid in, and never to a third party.

## 4. Clauses no longer in force

4.1 The clause providing that "An allowed claim is paid at the lower of the amount allowed and the benefit limit that applies to it, less the deductible that applies to it." is **no longer in force**; what an allowed claim is paid is settled on the current basis for a settlement and not by this note.

4.2 The clause providing that "the total withheld across all claims on one policy never exceeds the plan's policy deductible ceiling" is likewise **no longer in force**; how the ceiling bears on what is withheld is settled on the current basis and not by this note.

4.3 The clauses of sections 1 to 3 stand as clauses in force, and the plan figures this note reads — the benefit limits, the benefit deductibles, the general deductible, the policy deductible ceiling and the reimbursement share for a cancel-for-any-reason claim — are valid as scheduled.

## 5. Reading the limits

On a certificate naming three travellers, a benefit stated as an amount per insured traveller stands at that amount for each of the three. A benefit stated as a share of the declared trip cost is one figure for the certificate, because the declared trip cost is one figure for the certificate.

An inner ceiling does not add to the benefit it sits within. Where a baggage benefit carries a ceiling on any single article, that ceiling caps what any one article may draw, and the benefit limit still caps the whole.

Because limits are consumed across the term, a certificate that has already paid part of a benefit in this term brings a smaller remaining limit to the next claim on it, and that remaining limit is not restored when the term merely runs on.

superseded_clauses: An allowed claim is paid at the lower of the amount allowed and the benefit limit that applies to it, less the deductible that applies to it.
the total withheld across all claims on one policy never exceeds the plan's policy deductible ceiling
